question: Do frozen UNICOM B/16 block-11 patch tokens contain enough complementary part correspondence to improve compact head retrieval before training a side branch?
population: SOP TRAIN seed179019 identity-disjoint holdout: 5,851 query/gallery images from 1,132 products, leave-one-out, no official test bytes; this split has been reused and is exploratory
control: frozen pretrained UNICOM B/16@224 with SOP TRAIN ArcFace-trained 768-to-128 head; 130-byte signed-int8/f16 deployed scorer; must reproduce 84.6009229% holdout Recall@1 and 0.6036782664 mAP@R
candidate: for each query, take the control's top 32 gallery rows, then rerank only those 32 by symmetric mean-of-max cosine between unit-normalized 196x768 frozen block-11 patch-token grids; exact ordinal ties; no training, no global-score blend, no extra serving artifact
metrics: holdout-only Recall@1 and mAP@R with per-query vectors, plus positive-in-top32 upper bound, paired 10,000-draw seed179019 product bootstrap for Recall@1 delta, maxsim wall time, CUDA peak and host RSS
advance_gate: only if candidate minus control Recall@1 is at least +1.0 percentage point, product-bootstrap 95% lower endpoint >0, and mAP@R has no point regression should the token-signal side-branch training hypothesis advance; otherwise kill this top32 MaxSim teacher recipe; do not infer a general token-information ceiling
scope: a deliberately cheap signal falsifier, not a deployable system or a SOTA/novelty claim; prior Cars/CUB local-token methods failed and this SOP result cannot erase those negatives
compute_estimate: 5,851 x 32 token-pair comparisons, each 196x196x768 MAC, about 5.5e12 MAC; GPU normalized heldout token tensor 3.5 GB float32 plus temporary batches; actual latency and memory must be measured
